He verbally committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[University of Massachusetts Amherst|UMass]], choosing them over Villanova, Maryland, Georgetown, and George Mason.[https://assets.espn.go.com/highschool/a/000823umass.html UMass gets Basden] He was released from his letter of intent following the resignation of Minutemen head coach [[Bruiser Flint]],[https://www.espn.com/recruiting/s/2001/0423/1184850.html Duquesne, 'Nova land top big men][https://web.archive.org/web/20110629113931/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/college/2002/ncaa_preview/nad/ Charlotte 49ers (2001: 22–11)] and Basden then committed to play for [[University of North Carolina at Charlotte|Charlotte]]. During his career with the 49ers, he was named [[Conference USA]] Player of the Year in 2005 and Defensive Player of the Year in 2004 and 2005. In his senior season, he was also named National Defensive Player of the Year by many college basketball analysts. He is the Conference USA all-time leader in career steals,{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120720181404/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=250402429|title=Charlotte 91, Houston 71}} and holds the all-time Charlotte record for steals.[https://web.archive.org/web/20050326195018/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=250430139 Charlotte 83, St. Louis 78 (OT)] His #13 jersey was retired on February 19, 2009.[https://web.archive.org/web/20090222055632/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290502429 Xavier falls to Charlotte in third straight road loss] ==Professional career== Basden went undrafted in the [[2005 NBA draft]] but was invited to play on the [[Chicago Bulls]] [[Reebok]] Summer League team, where a strong performance earned him a two-year contract with the Bulls. He appeared in 19 games for the Bulls in [[2005-06 NBA season|2005–06]], averaging 2.1 points per game. On August 18, 2006, Basden was traded by the Bulls to the Cleveland Cavaliers for center [[Martynas Andriuskevicius]]. He was later signed by [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] of Turkey. He averaged 8.4 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 3.3 assists in 25 minutes for Fenerbahçe in the [[Euroleague]] and was a key player in the team's 2007 [[Turkish Basketball League]] championship. Basden later played for the [[Austin Toros]] of the [[NBA D-League]].[http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/index.jsp?player=eddie_basden Eddie Basden D-League profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100221023403/http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/index.jsp?player=eddie_basden |date=2010-02-21 }} After finishing his contract with the Toros, he went to play for the [[Alaska Aces (PBA)|Alaska Aces]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]], but was ultimately rejected for exceeding the league's {{height|ft=6|in=4}} height limit.[http://www.gmanews.tv/story/211925/history-repeats-itself-alaskas-pba-import-exceeds-height-limit History repeats itself: Alaska's PBA import exceeds height limit], ''gmanews.tv''. Retrieved February 19, 2011. In March 2011, he signed with [[Maroussi BC]] in Greece.[http://www.sport.gr/default.asp?pid=4&aid=89073 Μπάσντεν ο αντι-Χουέρτας στο Μαρούσι] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721083248/http://www.sport.gr/default.asp?pid=4&aid=89073 |date=2011-07-21 }} {{in lang|el}} In October 2011 he signed with [[Franca Basquetebol Clube]] in Brazil.[https://www.latinbasket.com/Brazil/basketball.aspx?NewsID=245663 Franca sign Edward Eddie Basden] In 2012, he signed as an import with the [[Petron Blaze Boosters]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]].{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20120518210623/http://www.pba-online.net/pba/Petron-confident-with-full-lineup/9367/ Petron confident with full lineup]}} He later played for various teams in Latin America.[http://basketball.latinbasket.com/player/Edward_Basden/San_Carlos/46947 Eddie Basden].
